Retain the entries where a host's needs and a culture's growth did not agree. Coexistence was work, not a recovered natural harmony.
completion: The corrected archive separates chemical signaling from orders and individual experience from a whole lineage. Oru leaves space for the parts biology has not yet explained. One diarist chose a weaker culture to keep breathing through winter. Oru refuses to edit the compromise into a story of perfect partnership.

title: Where the Air Goes
briefing: A clinic plans to vent a culture room onto an upper walkway. Survey the airflow and public access so its new system can contain experimental spores without isolating ordinary Sporebound residents from the city around them.
completion: A filtered vent route protects the walkway. The clinic's safety plan applies to the experiment rather than to everyone who shares a lineage with its patients.

title: Green under the White
briefing: At the Brine Bloom's seep, industrial strains are escaping into the salt pans. Visit the boundary and compare living color with the suppliers' restoration claims. Oru wants a survey of who can survive this growth, not a photograph proving that something green exists.
completion: The fans are thriving where native communities and human households are failing. The supplier calls every new patch recovery. Oru records the losses alongside the spread; nature has not chosen a side anyone can inhabit without cost.

title: The Culture That Ate Its Neighbors
briefing: Read the Brine Bloom culture bank's mineral records. The licensed strain was bred to depend on a scarce feed; its feral descendants learned to draw from the seep instead. The response needs to distinguish an ended monopoly from an ecosystem made safe.
completion: The patent's hold is weaker and the pressure on the seep is greater. Oru marks the remaining refuges without promising that one emancipated organism will leave room for another.

title: No Blanket Cure
briefing: Continuance's treatment drones are spraying a broad sterilant that harms the refuges along with the industrial strain. Disable the spray units before their simple solution destroys the diversity the response is supposed to protect.
completion: The spray front stops at the marked boundary. The clinic replaces its borrowed pesticide plan with targeted removal and carefully contained trials.

title: The Patient Bioreactor
briefing: Configure a sealed bioreactor at the forge to test mixed cultures against the industrial strain. Include their water draw and waste heat in the comparison. A counter-culture that wins by consuming the last reserve would merely give the collapse another name.
completion: One mixed community slows the strain, but only while receiving nutrients the wider basin cannot supply. The result is useful inside a bounded refuge. Oru refuses the proposed headline announcing a cure.

title: The Quarantine Line
briefing: Wardens enforce an old industrial quarantine against Sporebound travelers while ignoring unsealed company sample crates. Disable the discriminatory checkpoint so inspectors can apply containment rules to actual materials and exposures.
completion: Travelers regain the route, and the sample crates finally receive inspection. The new boundary follows a documented hazard instead of a person's ancestry.

title: A Library That Stays in Its Jars
briefing: Register a diverse, sealed culture library at the Brine Bloom bank, with a limited water allowance and withdrawal boundary. The keepers can preserve samples and protect narrow refuges; they cannot restore the whole salt pan by releasing another organism with orders to win.
completion: The library opens. Families outside its defensible boundary receive relocation notices and a share of the remaining supplies. Nobody confuses the safety of the jars with the recovery of the place they came from.

title: The Pact Nobody Else Signed
briefing: Walk the Brine Bloom's remaining seep after the contained trials. Confirm the refuge boundary and record the growth beyond it, including the strains that now live without a supplier. Oru asks for a conclusion that does not turn survival into innocence or diversity into a promise of peace.
completion: The monopoly is broken. A few cultures remain in common care, and the wild bloom continues across the evacuated pans. Hosts and fungi keep negotiating needs that cannot all be met. The pact is an agreement among the people still here. Nothing in the salt has signed it, and nothing promises to wait for their next decision.

title: The Water beneath the Wage
briefing: Mara Venn tends the pumps in Mourning Fen, east of Vesper. Her wage buys her father clean water from the same concession that drains his well. Read the drawdown gauge among the reeds; she needs a measurement the company cannot dismiss as a family grievance.
completion: The water falls fastest during the shifts that pay best. Mara recognizes the dates on her overtime slips. The reeds have been absorbing poison for free; when they die, the company will sell another filter.

title: A Share in the Thirst
briefing: The sluice register offers pump families shares instead of unpaid wages. The dividend rises whenever extraction exceeds the wetland limit. Mara asks you to retrieve the contract before her crew signs away the last reason to slow the pumps.
completion: The shares carry no vote, only an interest in the damage. Mara had hoped that ownership would make the workers safer. The contract would make their hunger another reason to empty the fen.

title: Enough for This Winter
briefing: Mara has negotiated a lower draw limit and a winter wage floor, funded by canceling the concession dividend. Record the settlement at the sluice. It protects the remaining reed beds, but leaves the contaminated pools untreated and lets the lease resume when the wage guarantee expires.
completion: The pump slows. Mara can buy her father water through winter; she cannot promise spring. The concession calls its smaller withdrawal sustainable. At the gauge, the old high-water stain stays above your head.

title: The Forest in the Prospectus
briefing: Tovin Ash cuts timber in Cinderwood, west of Vesper. A restoration fund pays for every dead trunk removed and sells credit for the seedlings meant to replace it. Check the stump ledger: his crew has been asked to fell living trees to keep the recovery figures rising.
completion: Every seedling has already been sold as a mature tree. Most have not survived their first dry season. Tovin shows you the clean nursery photograph used on every certificate; it is the same photograph, taken eleven years ago.

title: What the Canopy Keeps
briefing: Tovin once signed the false certificates because the fund paid for his daughter's lung treatment. Visit the last canopy refuge and record the damp soil under the living trees. Taking those trees would finish his debt and expose the seedlings to the heat that already killed their neighbors.
completion: The ground under the canopy is cool enough to hold water. Beyond its edge, roots crumble between your fingers. Tovin's daughter asks him to stop cutting. Her next treatment invoice arrives before he can answer.

title: A Common without a Surplus
briefing: The cutters will take the surviving wood into common care and sell only fallen timber. Enter their actual yield and treatment debts in the ledger, canceling the invented restoration credits. Shared ownership can end the payout for destruction; it cannot make the dead forest produce a living wage.
completion: The certificates lose their value. So does the crew's pension reserve, which the fund invested in them. Tovin keeps his daughter's appointment by selling his tools. The canopy survives this season. No one calls the account balanced.

title: A Body in the Seam
briefing: Ada Silt fires replacement plates for Lattice patients on the northern Glassroot Steppe. The mineral seam beneath the grasses is almost spent. Read the soil core before approving a deeper cut; Ada's partner needs a new shell, and the settlement needs the roots holding its well in place.
completion: The seam continues beneath the root mat. Removing it would keep the kiln supplied for years and collapse the well within months. Ada presses a cracked plate against the core sample. Both are irreplaceable on the schedule she has been given.

title: Vacant Means Unprofitable
briefing: The land register marks the steppe vacant because neither the grass nor its remaining households pay ground rent. Retrieve the survey used to authorize the mine. Ada wants the families counted before a reclamation crew mistakes their homes for material left by the dead.
completion: The surveyor recorded every home and then removed them from the valuation. Their existence was never in doubt; only their purchasing power was. The same company offers the families relocation loans secured against their next address.

title: An Address after the Grass
briefing: Ada's settlement has accepted a public relocation grant with no repayment clause. Record the retreat and close the deeper extraction claim. Salvaged ceramic will cover urgent repairs, while everyone else waits longer. The families keep the right to return to land that may no longer support them.
completion: The register records residents and then records their departure. Ada carries her partner's patched shell south on a handcart. Grass moves through the abandoned kiln. It has not forgiven the settlement; it has no use for forgiveness.

title: The Green That Came Back Wrong
briefing: Ilex Marr watches fungal fans spread across the southern Brine Bloom. Investors call the color a recovered ecosystem; the families driven out by its spores call it another eviction. Inspect the last freshwater seep before the bloom drinks the refuge cultures dry.
completion: The licensed strain and its feral descendants consume the same seep. Both are living things. Neither distinguishes a nursery, a lung, or a competitor when it finds somewhere to grow. Recovery is a word being spoken over their chemistry.

title: A Patent with No Heirs
briefing: The culture bank's owner is gone, but Continuance still charges hosts for every propagated strain. Read the oldest custody record. Ilex needs to separate the right to keep a partner alive from the instruction to keep multiplying it until the lease earns enough.
completion: The strain was designed to require scarce nutrients, keeping its hosts tied to a supplier. Escaped descendants shed that dependence and began consuming the seep. Freedom from the patent did not teach the fungus restraint.

title: Leave Something Unclaimed
briefing: Ilex will cancel the propagation lease, keep diverse cultures sealed, and withdraw the outer settlement instead of sterilizing the whole bloom. Register the boundary and the remaining supplies. This refusal leaves room for other life; it also leaves homes behind and binds the keepers to years of containment.
completion: The bank stops selling a future it cannot supply. Beyond its seals, growth covers the empty houses. Ilex keeps one lamp for the next inspection. The basin will go on changing after the lamp fails. It offers no assurance that anyone will be here to name the change.
